1	# Multi-Team Support
2	
3	Each player or group gets their own MTS team — an independent force with its own research and its own copy of the map — so people share one server and one start but race to different finishes. Exposes the `mts-v1` remote interface so companion mods can extend the multi-team experience.
4	
5	> This glossary is seeded from the MTS Dimension Warp design session and covers only the terms that came up there. Grow it as other areas are documented.
6	
7	## Language
8	
9	**Team**:
10	A force named `team-N` with independent research, relations, and surfaces. The unit of isolation — one member leads, others may join or buddy up.
11	_Avoid_: clan, group (in code)
12	
13	**Team surface**:
14	A surface owned by a team — its home-planet variant, an outer planet, or a space platform. Ownership is tracked by MTS, not inferred from the surface name alone.
15	
16	**Home surface**:
17	The team surface a player spawns onto, and is bounced back to if they stray onto a surface they don't own.
18	
19	**Landing pen**:
20	A shared lobby surface where new players stage — on the spectator force, not yet on a team — until they claim or join one.
21	_Avoid_: lobby, waiting room
22	
23	**Spectator**:
24	A player temporarily moved to the spectator force to watch teams, and restored to their real team on exit.
25	
26	**Pause**:
27	Freezing a team so it makes no progress: power generation is disabled across all of the team's surfaces (the airtight freeze), and pole wires are recorded and cut for the Space-Age visual thaw. A consumer-driven capability (e.g. MTS Dimension Warp's docking bay) — MTS does not offer it on its own, because a paused base has no powered defenses and is only safe somewhere a consumer has already made safe.

2	name: chat-message-style
3	description: Coding conventions for player-facing chat messages and GUI labels in the Multi-Team Support Factorio mod. Covers player name colorization and force name tagging.
4	---
5	
6	# Chat Message & GUI Style Guide
7	
8	When writing or modifying any player-facing messages (via `player.print`, `helpers.broadcast`, or GUI labels), follow these two rules strictly.
9	
10	## Rule 1: Player names must always be colorized
11	
12	Never use `player.name` directly in a player-visible message. Always wrap it with `helpers.colored_name()` using the player's `chat_color`:
13	
14	```lua
15	-- WRONG
16	target.print(requester.name .. " has joined your team.")
17	
18	-- CORRECT
19	target.print(helpers.colored_name(requester.name, requester.chat_color) .. " has joined your team.")
20	```
21	
22	`helpers.colored_name(name, color)` produces Factorio rich text: `[color=R,G,B]name[/color]`
23	
24	When you have the player object, use `player.chat_color`. If you only have a name string, look up the player first:
25	```lua
26	local p = game.get_player(name)
27	if p then helpers.colored_name(p.name, p.chat_color) end
28	```
29	
30	**Applies to:** `player.print()`, `helpers.broadcast()`, GUI labels that mention player names.
31	
32	**Does NOT apply to:** `log()` calls (debug only, not shown to players), tooltips, or internal identifiers.
33	
34	## Rule 2: Force name tag must appear after every mention of "team"
35	
36	Whenever a message mentions the word "team" (your team, the team, team leader, former team, etc.), append a grey force-name tag using `helpers.force_tag()`:
37	
38	```lua
39	-- WRONG
40	caller.print("You have left the team.")
41	
42	-- CORRECT
43	caller.print("You have left the team." .. helpers.force_tag(caller.force.name))
44	```
45	
46	`helpers.force_tag(force_name)` produces: ` [color=0.50,0.50,0.50](force-bob)[/color]`
47	
48	The force tag always goes at the **end of the sentence**, after the period.
49	
50	### Examples of correct messages:
51	
52	```lua
53	-- Team join
54	requester.print("You joined " .. cn_target .. "'s team." .. helpers.force_tag(target.force.name))
55	
56	-- Team leave
57	member.print(cn_player .. " has left the team." .. ft)
58	
59	-- Team leader change
60	member.print(cn_leader .. " is now the team leader." .. ft)
61	
62	-- Broadcast
63	helpers.broadcast("[Team] " .. cn_leader .. " now leads " .. cn_player .. "'s former team." .. ft)
64	
65	-- Kick
66	target.print("You have been kicked from the team by " .. cn_caller .. "." .. ft)
67	
68	-- Team full
69	requester.print(cn_target .. "'s team is full." .. helpers.force_tag(target.force.name))
70	```
71	
72	### Common pattern — cache both for readability:
73	
74	```lua
75	local cn_player = helpers.colored_name(player.name, player.chat_color)
76	local ft = helpers.force_tag(old_force_name)
77	member.print(cn_player .. " has left the team." .. ft)
78	```
79	
80	## In the Players GUI (surfaces_gui)
81	
82	The Players GUI shows the force name in grey brackets next to each owner name:
83	
84	```lua
85	if info.force_name then
86	    local force_lbl = owner_flow.add{type = "label", caption = " [" .. info.force_name .. "]"}
87	    force_lbl.style.font       = "default-small"
88	    force_lbl.style.font_color = {0.5, 0.5, 0.5}
89	end
90	```
91	
92	## Helper functions reference
93	
94	| Function | Location | Purpose |
95	|----------|----------|---------|
96	| `helpers.colored_name(name, color)` | `helpers.lua` | Wraps a name in `[color]...[/color]` rich text |
97	| `helpers.force_tag(force_name)` | `helpers.lua` | Returns grey ` (force-name)` suffix for chat messages |
98	| `helpers.colored_name` + `helpers.force_tag` | Combined | Standard pattern for all team-related messages |

1	# 🏭 Multi-Team Support
2	
3	> **Same start. Different finish.**
4	
5	A Factorio 2.0 mod for cooperative and competitive multiplayer where each team races on their own copy of the world. Research independently, compare progress, watch your rivals, form alliances — all from one server.
6	
7	> **Inspired by OARC.** Multi-Team Support carries the same many-players-one-server spirit as the OARC separated-spawns mods, reimagined for Factorio 2.0 with a full per-team copy of the world.
8	
9	> **Note on tooling:** This mod is developed with AI coding assistants alongside human review and in-game testing. Bug reports, feature requests, and contributions are welcome from everyone. If AI-assisted development isn't your thing, that's fine — but please keep the hate off this mod's threads. And a gentle request: please don't be rude or disrespectful to the author on other platforms either. There's a human on the other side, don't be anti-human by being rude to them.
10	
11	## 💬 Community
12	
13	Join the Discord: https://discord.gg/tWz4FT74pH
14	
15	## ✨ Features
16	
17	### Teams
18	- 🧑‍🚀 **Numbered team pool** — Forces pre-created as `team-1` through `team-N` (configurable via startup setting, default 20). Team names are display-only and can be renamed via `/mts-rename` or the Teams panel.
19	- 👥 **Multi-player teams** — Buddy join lets multiple players share a team. Leader can kick and accept join requests; any member can leave.
20	- 🎨 **Force colors** — Always derived from the current team leader's player color.
21	- 🤝 **Friendship** — Two-sided requests between teams; mutual friendship shares chart and grants friend-view spectation.
22	- 📡 **Passive radars** — Radars keep the area around them visible but no longer run the rotating scan that permanently charts the wider map; the standard radar also draws less power (50 kW instead of 300 kW, modded radars keep their own cost). On a multi-team server, 20 teams each carpeting their territory with map-charting radars is a major save-size and UPS sink; this bounds that growth while keeping the local visibility players place radars for. **On by default**; disable via startup setting *Passive radars (no map scanning)*. It only stops further charting — already-charted map stays charted — and purpose-built scanner buildings from other mods are left untouched.
23	
24	### 🌌 Space Age Integration *(auto-detected)*
25	- 🪐 **Per-team planet variants** — When Space Age is active, each team gets their own full solar system. The vanilla 5 (Nauvis, Vulcanus, Gleba, Fulgora, Aquilo) plus any modded planets registered via `data:extend` or planet libraries like PlanetsLib (Maraxsis, Lignumis, Muluna, etc.) all get per-team variants automatically. No collisions on shared planets.
26	- 🛸 **Per-team space connections** — Whatever topology exists in the loaded mod stack is mirrored per team, so rocket launches and space platforms work per-team across vanilla and modded planets alike.
27	- 🔒 **Base planets locked** — Team forces only see/reach their own variants. Discovery techs unlock the team's variant, not the base. Detection scans for `unlock-space-location` effects on every loaded technology, so modded discovery techs route correctly regardless of naming convention.
28	- 📦 Falls back to surface-cloning when Space Age isn't installed — same experience, just no orbits.
29	
30	### 🏆 Records & Announcements
31	- 🥇 **Tech records** — First team to research any tech gets an announcement. Subsequent faster researches (measured from each team's clock) broadcast new speed records.
32	- 📈 **Milestone engine** — Configurable production thresholds per category (science packs, landfill, space platform tiles). Edit `milestones/config.lua` to add more. Dynamic item discovery handles any mod combo.
33	- ⏱️ **Team clock** — Starts when the first member spawns; never resets. Makes speed comparisons fair regardless of when a team joined.
34	- 📢 **Server announcements** — New players receive a welcome with the Discord invite link; returning players get a welcome-back that includes their team name. A server-wide Discord reminder broadcasts every 6 hours. The URL is configured via Settings → Map → Discord URL (defaults to the community Discord; leave blank to disable).
35	
36	### 🖥️ GUI Panels *(top-left toolbar)*
37	- 🗂️ **Teams** — Card per team showing the active research queue (up to 7 icons with live progress bars), a colour-coded last-active indicator with per-player playtime on hover, members (★ leader, online/offline, 🤝 friendship, 📡 Follow Cam per player) and surfaces (👁 Spectate).
38	- 📡 **Follow Cam** — Grid of live mini-cameras tracking individual players across planets. Click the 🔍 on any cell to expand into full spectator view; Esc returns with the grid intact.
39	- 🔬 **Research** — Tech icon grid ordered by research time. Click any team for a 1-on-1 diff.
40	- 📊 **Production Stats** — Per-team item production comparison with per-player item tracking and sortable columns.
41	- 🛠️ **Admin Panel** — Runtime feature flags, starter items editor, and team size limit. Toolbar button is admin-only.
42	- 👋 **Welcome / Discord** — Mod intro + Discord invite with scannable QR code.
43	
44	### 🛬 Landing Pen
45	- New players wait in a shared pre-game lobby until ready to spawn.
46	- **"Start a new team"** or **"Request to join"** an existing team — other actions disable while a join request is pending.
47	- Request flow and join/leave events announce to all connected players (only the leader can accept).
48	- Withdraw a request at any time with the Cancel button.
49	
50	### ⚡ Commands
51	- `/t <message>` — Send a private message to your team only (other teams see nothing).
52	- `/mts-teams` — List all teams with leader and member counts, colored by team color.
53	- `/mts-players` — List all players and their surfaces with GPS pings.
54	- `/mts-leave` — Leave your team (confirmation dialog explains consequences).
55	- `/mts-kick <player>` — Kick a player from your team (leader only, with confirmation).
56	- `/mts-rename <name>` — Rename your team (leader only, 32 char limit, no duplicates).
57	
58	## ⚙️ Compatibility
59	
60	- Requires **Factorio 2.0** (`base >= 2.0`)
61	- **Space Age** — optional; auto-detected and enables per-team planets + space connections when present
62	- Compatible with [Platformer](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/platformer)
63	- **Companion modes** *(optional — built on the `mts-v1` API, each plays out independently per team)*:
64	  - [**Diggy**](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/diggy) — the world is solid rock; dig out your factory, brace the ceilings, and survive cave-ins. First-class MTS integration: every team races an identically-seeded dig world.
65	  - **MTS Expanse** — tiny-island Expanse gameplay: feed hungry chests, unlock land, race teams, and survive invasions.
66	  - **Brave New MTS** — a remote-only, character-free layer: your character never leaves its cell; you build entirely through a construction-robot network seeded at each team's spawn.
67	- **open-discord-bridge (ODB)** — optional; relays per-team announcements, milestones, and chat to a Discord channel.
68	- **Generic terrain mirror** — any third-party mod that decorates Nauvis via `on_chunk_generated` (and filters by hardcoded surface name) is automatically mirrored onto every team surface. The mod's handler runs once on the real Nauvis; MTS clones the resulting tiles, entities, and decoratives to each team's nauvis variant. Verified working with [dangOreus](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/dangOreus), [VoidBlock](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/VoidBlock), [Alien Biomes](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/alien-biomes), and content mods like [Periodic Madness](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/periodic-madness). Trade-off: every team gets the same map (per-team randomization is sacrificed for zero-cooperation compat). See [`docs/COMPAT.md`](docs/COMPAT.md) for details.
69	- **dangOreus** — beyond the terrain mirror, MTS also reproduces dangOreus's runtime gameplay rules (block non-miners on ore tiles, spill containers on death, floor-is-lava damage) on team surfaces.
70	- **Krastorio 2 / Krastorio 2 Spaced Out** — crash-site entities (vanilla wrecks + K2 spaceship pieces) on team Nauvis surfaces are normalised to `force=neutral` so teams can mine them; team forces are kept at war with `kr-internal-turrets` so K2's planetary teleporter "standing on" detection and tesla coil targeting fire correctly on team characters.
71	- Factorio supports up to 64 forces. Without Space Age: up to 60 teams (64 minus 4 reserved built-in forces). With Space Age: capped at 20 due to per-team planet variant pre-creation.
72	
73	## 🔌 For Mod Authors
74	
75	Multi-Team Support exposes a public remote interface (`mts-v1`) and custom events so other mods can integrate cleanly without per-mod compatibility shims.
76	
77	```lua
78	-- Subscribe to a custom event
79	if remote.interfaces["mts-v1"] then
80	    local id = remote.call("mts-v1", "get_event_id", "on_team_surface_created")
81	    script.on_event(id, function(event)
82	        -- event.surface_name, event.force_name
83	    end)
84	end
85	
86	-- Query state
87	local owner = remote.call("mts-v1", "get_surface_owner", "team-3-nauvis")

89	```
90	
91	**Events:** `on_team_created`, `on_team_released`, `on_player_joined_team`, `on_player_left_team`, `on_team_surface_created`.
92	
93	**Queries:** `get_team_list`, `get_team_info`, `is_team_surface`, `get_surface_owner`, `list_team_surfaces`.

95	The interface name is versioned (`mts-v1`); breaking changes will ship as a parallel `mts-v2` rather than mutating v1. 1	# Multi-Team Support: Integration API
2	
3	This document covers MTS-specific integration points: how MTS handles third-party chunk-gen mods automatically and the public `mts-v1` remote interface (events + queries).
4	
5	For *generic* advice on making your mod work in any multi-force environment (not specific to MTS), see [COMPAT.md](COMPAT.md). This document assumes your mod is already reasonably force- and surface-aware, and you want to plug into MTS lifecycle directly.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Terrain mirroring (no integration needed)
10	
11	MTS gives every team its own copy of each planet:
12	
13	- Space Age: `mts-<planet>-<N>` (e.g. `mts-nauvis-3`, `mts-vulcanus-3`)
14	- Base 2.0 (no Space Age): `team-<N>-<planet>` (e.g. `team-3-nauvis`)
15	
16	When a chunk is generated on any team surface, MTS automatically:
17	
18	1. Generates the matching chunk on the *real* planet surface (`nauvis`, `vulcanus`, …), synchronously firing every third-party mod's `on_chunk_generated` handler. Their `surface.name == "nauvis"` filters accept, their decoration runs.
19	2. Mirrors the resulting tiles, entities, and decoratives from the real planet to the team surface via `LuaSurface.clone_area`.
20	
21	Implementation: [`compat/clone_mirror.lua`](../compat/clone_mirror.lua).
22	
23	Net effect: whatever your mod puts on a real planet, every team's variant gets the same. No remote interface to wire up, no surface-name predicate to update, no MTS-aware code path required. Works for vanilla and modded planets equally — the pattern strips the `mts-` / `team-N-` prefix and uses whatever planet name your mod registered.
24	
25	**Verified working with:** [dangOreus](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/dangOreus), [VoidBlock](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/VoidBlock), [Alien Biomes](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/alien-biomes), [Periodic Madness](https://mods.factorio.com/mod/periodic-madness), and the vanilla worldgen stack.
26	
27	### When mirroring isn't enough
28	
29	Some mods don't only decorate at chunk-gen. They also have **runtime rules** that fire later — `on_built_entity`, `on_entity_died`, `on_nth_tick`, etc. — and filter those handlers by `surface.name == "nauvis"`. Mirroring gives you the *terrain*; it doesn't make those runtime rules fire on the mirrored terrain.
30	
31	For those, see Pattern 5 in [COMPAT.md](COMPAT.md) ("Expose runtime rules so other mods can reuse them") or the `mts-v1` event subscription below.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. The `mts-v1` remote interface
36	
37	A stable, versioned API for mods that want first-class awareness of MTS lifecycle. Source: [`scripts/remote_api.lua`](../scripts/remote_api.lua).
38	
39	**Stability contract:** the interface name `mts-v1` and every function/event listed below is frozen for the v1 lifetime. Adding new functions/events is safe; renaming or removing is not. Breaking changes will ship as a parallel `mts-v2` rather than mutating v1. Always guard your calls with `if remote.interfaces["mts-v1"] then ...` so your mod stays compatible across MTS versions and works in saves where MTS is absent.
40	
41	### 2.1 Events
42	
43	Custom events you can subscribe to:
44	
45	| Event name                  | Payload fields                          | Raised when                                   |
46	|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
47	| `on_team_created`           | `force_name`, `player_index` (leader)   | A team slot is claimed and the force is set up |
48	| `on_team_released`          | `force_name`                            | A team slot is released (team disbanded)       |
49	| `on_team_surface_created`   | `surface_name`, `force_name`            | A new team surface (planet variant) is created |
50	| `on_player_joined_team`     | `player_index`, `force_name`            | A player moves onto a team force               |
51	| `on_player_left_team`       | `player_index`, `force_name`            | A player leaves a team force                   |
52	| `on_team_clock_started`     | `force_name`, `start_tick`              | A team's clock starts (team has started playing) — fires once, on direct claim or on the staged-start "Start Playing" commit |
53	| `on_team_renamed`           | `force_name`, `new_name`                | A team is renamed (refresh anything showing the team name) |
54	| `on_team_tab_built`         | `player_index`, `tab_name`, `element`   | A player's Team Settings panel is (re)built — once per registered custom tab; `element` is the empty content frame to populate |
55	| `on_welcome_tab_built`      | `player_index`, `tab_name`, `element`   | The welcome screen is (re)built — once per registered welcome tab; `element` is the empty content frame to populate |
56	| `on_platform_hub_gui_built` | `player_index`, `widget_name`, `element`, `entity` | A player opens a space platform hub — once per registered widget; `element` is the anchored content frame, `entity` the hub |
57	| `on_starter_items_added`    | `items` (`{name=, count=}` list)        | An admin adds starter items while a delivery override is registered — the override consumer must deliver them |
58	
59	The last four events pair with the registration functions in §2.4: register a tab / widget / override once, then listen to the matching `*_built` / `*_added` event to fill the frame (or deliver the items) each time MTS raises it.
60	
61	Event IDs are generated per session via `script.generate_event_name()` — they're stable for the duration of a session but not across sessions, so always look them up via `get_event_id` rather than caching the integer.
62	
63	**Subscribing:**
64	
65	`remote.call` is **not** legal during `on_load`, yet event handlers must be registered in both `on_init` and `on_load` for determinism. Bridge the gap with a one-shot `on_nth_tick(1)` — it fires on the same tick for every peer (so it stays multiplayer-deterministic), and both `remote.call` and `script.on_event` are legal inside it:
66	
67	```lua
68	-- Resolve the event ID and register the real handler. Safe from a runtime
69	-- context (on_nth_tick / on_init), never from on_load.
70	local function subscribe_mts_events()
71	    if not remote.interfaces["mts-v1"] then return end
72	    local id = remote.call("mts-v1", "get_event_id", "on_team_surface_created")
73	    script.on_event(id, function(event)
74	        -- event.surface_name, event.force_name
75	        local surface = game.surfaces[event.surface_name]
76	        if surface then my_mod.setup_surface(surface, event.force_name) end
77	    end)
78	end
79	
80	-- Defer to the next tick so we can remote.call for the ID even on a load path.
81	-- Registering on_nth_tick itself is legal in on_load (no remote.call, no
82	-- storage write); the deferred body runs in a normal context.
83	local function defer_subscribe()
84	    script.on_nth_tick(1, function()
85	        script.on_nth_tick(1, nil)  -- one-shot: unregister after the first fire
86	        subscribe_mts_events()
87	    end)
88	end
89	
90	script.on_init(defer_subscribe)
91	script.on_load(defer_subscribe)
92	```
93	
94	The `on_team_surface_created` event is the most useful one for terrain/decoration mods that need to run setup exactly once per team surface (rather than reacting per-chunk). The `on_team_created` event is useful for force-level setup — granting starting research, applying buffs, etc.
95	
96	### 2.2 Queries
97	
98	Synchronous queries you can call any time:
99	
100	| Call                                                | Returns                                            |
101	|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
102	| `get_event_id(name)`                                | Event ID for the named event, or `nil`             |
103	| `get_team_list()`                                   | Array of team info tables (one per claimed slot)   |
104	| `get_team_info(force_name)`                         | Team info table, or `nil` if not a team force      |
105	| `is_team_surface(surface_name)`                     | `true` if the surface is owned by a team           |
106	| `get_surface_owner(surface_name)`                   | The owning team's `force_name`, or `nil`           |
107	| `list_team_surfaces(force_name)`                    | Array of surface names owned by that team          |
108	| `is_team_paused(force_name)`                        | `true` if the team is currently paused             |
109	| `is_team_online(force_name)`                        | `true` if any member is connected — counts a member spectating another team |
110	| `get_effective_force(player_index)`                 | The player's effective team `force_name` — their real team even while spectating another surface — or `nil` |
111	| `get_team_label(force_name)`                         | MTS-styled rich-text label (team's coloured tag + current leader in brackets), or `nil`. Reflects live state — re-fetch after a rename/leader/colour change |
112	| `get_starter_items()`                               | Array of admin-configured starter items (`{name=, count=}`), for a delivery-override consumer seeding teams that spawn later |
113	
114	### 2.3 Actions
115	
116	Functions that mutate world state. Call from a real event context (not `on_load`):
117	
118	| Call                                                | Effect                                                                                  |
119	|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
120	| `pause_team(force_name)`                            | Freeze the team: disable every power source (the airtight freeze), deactivate remaining entities via the amortized sweep, and (Space Age) cut pole wires for a visible "unplugged" look. Returns `true` if a pause started. |
121	| `unpause_team(force_name, opts)`                     | Resume the team: re-enable power sources, reactivate entities, and (Space Age) staggered-reconnect the pole wires so the lights ripple back. `opts = {mode, duration}` reserved for a future timed-pause v2. Returns `true` if a resume started. |
122	| `create_team_surface(force_name, spec)`             | Create (or look up) an ephemeral, caller-seeded surface for a team. `spec = {name, planet, map_gen_settings}` — `name` is **required** and must be non-variant (not `mts-<planet>-N` / `team-N-<planet>`); `planet` is used only for Space Age planet association; `map_gen_settings` carries the caller's seed. Returns the surface name, or `nil`. Works with or without Space Age. |
123	| `retire_team_surface(force_name, surface_name)`     | Delete a team-owned surface and unwind its bookkeeping. Returns `true` on success, `false` if the surface is invalid or not owned by that team. |
124	| `set_spawn_label_enabled(surface_name, enabled)`    | Suppress (`false`) or restore (`true`) MTS's default spawn label on a surface a consumer labels itself. |
125	| `disband_team(force_name)`                          | Disband a team: move every member back to the landing pen, release the slot, and clean up the team's surfaces. Use for a loss condition (e.g. a critical structure destroyed). |
126	| `ensure_passive_radar(force_name, surface, position)` | Ensure a hidden, powerless, non-charting passive radar exists so an empty team surface stays live-viewable for spectators. `surface` may be a name, index, or `LuaSurface`. Idempotent per `(surface, position)`; re-call after every surface clone. Returns the `LuaEntity`, or `nil` if the surface/force is invalid. |
127	
128	A `team_info` table has the following shape:
129	
130	```lua
131	{
132	    force_name           = "team-3",
133	    display_name         = "The Reds",     -- player-chosen name, or force_name
134	    status               = "occupied",      -- "occupied" | "available"
135	    is_occupied          = true,
136	    leader_player_index  = 7,
137	    member_count         = 4,
138	    is_paused            = false,
139	    clock_start_tick     = 1234,            -- tick the team's clock started
140	    online_ticks         = 98760,           -- total ticks a member has been online
141	}
142	```
143	
144	**Examples:**
145	
146	```lua
147	-- Is this surface owned by a team?
148	if remote.interfaces["mts-v1"]
149	   and remote.call("mts-v1", "is_team_surface", surface.name) then
150	    -- handle team-surface case
151	end
152	
153	-- Who owns this surface?
154	local owner = remote.call("mts-v1", "get_surface_owner", "mts-nauvis-3")
155	-- → "team-3" or nil
156	
157	-- All current teams:
158	for _, info in ipairs(remote.call("mts-v1", "get_team_list")) do
159	    game.print(info.display_name .. " has " .. info.member_count .. " members")
160	end
161	```
162	
163	### 2.4 Registration (call once, then listen)
164	
165	These extend MTS's own UI or milestone machinery. Register **once**, from your `on_init` **and** `on_configuration_changed` (where `remote.call` is legal and storage writes are allowed) — the registry persists in `storage`, so it survives save/load and stays identical on every peer. Re-registering the same `name` overwrites; it is safe to call on every config change.
166	
167	| Call                                                     | Effect                                                                                       |
168	|----------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
169	| `register_team_tab(spec)`                                | Add a tab to the Team Settings panel. `spec = {name, caption, order, mod}`. Then fill the frame handed to you by `on_team_tab_built`. |
170	| `register_welcome_tab(spec)`                             | Add a tab to the welcome screen (rendered **before** MTS's About/Discord; the first registered tab is selected by default). Same `spec` shape; listen to `on_welcome_tab_built`. |
171	| `register_platform_hub_widget(spec)`                     | Anchor a widget into the native space-platform-hub GUI. `spec = {name, caption, order, position, mod}` (`position` is a `relative_gui_position`, default `"right"`); listen to `on_platform_hub_gui_built`. |
172	| `register_starter_item_delivery(mod_name)`              | Take over delivery of the admin-configured starter items (MTS then stops inserting them into player inventories). Pass **your mod name** so the override self-clears if your mod is removed. Listen to `on_starter_items_added` for live additions and read `get_starter_items()` for teams that spawn later. |
173	| `register_milestone(spec)`                               | Define a consumer milestone. `spec = {category, verb, noun, first_threshold, thresholds}`. `first_threshold` (optional) gets a first-to-reach announcement only; each entry in `thresholds` gets both first **and** fastest. |
174	| `report_milestone(force_name, category, count)`         | Report a team's current counter for a registered milestone; MTS announces first/fastest via the same records + broadcast + Discord path as its built-in milestones. Event-driven — call it as the counter advances, don't poll. |
175	
176	**Include a `mod` field** (your mod name) in any `register_team_tab` / `register_welcome_tab` / `register_platform_hub_widget` spec: MTS sweeps registrations whose owning mod was removed on the next `on_configuration_changed`. Entries registered without a `mod` field persist indefinitely.
177	
178	```lua
179	-- Register a Team Settings tab, then populate it when MTS builds it.
180	local function register_mts_ui()
181	    if not remote.interfaces["mts-v1"] then return end
182	    remote.call("mts-v1", "register_team_tab",
183	        { name = "my-mod", caption = "My Mod", order = "z", mod = "my-mod" })
184	end
185	script.on_init(register_mts_ui)
186	script.on_configuration_changed(register_mts_ui)
187	
188	-- Fill the content frame each time the panel is (re)built (subscribe via the
189	-- deferred one-shot from §2.1).
190	local function on_tab_built(event)
191	    if event.tab_name ~= "my-mod" then return end
192	    event.element.add{ type = "label", caption = "Hello from my mod" }
193	end
194	```
195	
196	### 2.5 Choosing between mirroring, events, and queries
197	
198	| You want to…                                          | Use                                                      |
199	|-------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
200	| Put the same terrain on every team's planet           | Nothing — mirroring handles it automatically             |
201	| Run per-surface setup once (not per-chunk)            | `on_team_surface_created` event                          |
202	| Grant starting items / research to each new team      | `on_team_created` event                                  |
203	| React when a player joins or leaves a team            | `on_player_joined_team` / `on_player_left_team`          |
204	| Check "is this a team surface?" inside another handler| `is_team_surface` query                                  |
205	| Walk all active teams (e.g. for a scoreboard)         | `get_team_list` query                                    |
206	| Add your own UI to Team Settings / welcome / hub      | `register_team_tab` / `register_welcome_tab` / `register_platform_hub_widget` + the matching `*_built` event |
207	| Announce your own per-team milestones                 | `register_milestone` + `report_milestone`                |
208	
209	---
210	
211	## 3. Mods added to an existing save
212	
213	MTS makes one promise about timing, and it deliberately matches vanilla: **lifecycle events fire for every team and surface created from the moment the mod is installed onward.** A mod added mid-save takes effect on subsequently-created teams and surfaces, not retroactively on ones that already exist.
214	
215	This is the same boundary Factorio itself enforces — adding a worldgen or decoration mod to a running save does not redecorate already-generated chunks. MTS does not promise more than the base game, and there is **no admin command** to force retroactive setup.
216	
217	Why there's no retroactive mechanism:
218	
219	- **It can't help the mods that need it most.** A handler that filters `surface.name == "nauvis"` rejects a re-fired event exactly as it rejects the live one — no event trick can spoof `LuaSurface.name`. Those mods need a real fix (generalize the filter, or subscribe to `on_team_surface_created`), not a replay.
220	- **Retroactive grants are wrong, not just unsafe.** Re-firing `on_team_created` against a team that's been playing for hours would dump a starting kit onto an established base. New teams get their setup live; existing teams correctly don't.
221	
222	So: write your integration against the `mts-v1` events (§2) and it works for every team created while your mod is installed. If you need a mod's terrain on surfaces that predate its install, regenerate those surfaces (recycle the slot) — the same answer vanilla gives.
223	
224	---
225	
226	## 4. What MTS will not do
227	
228	- **Reverse-engineer or monkey-patch closed-source mods.** Fragile, version-coupled, breaks silently when upstream updates.
229	- **Spoof `surface.name`.** Not technically possible, and would lie to every other mod on the server.
230	- **Maintain compat shims for every mod that decorates a planet.** The terrain mirror handles the chunk-gen layer generically. Per-mod shims exist only for runtime rules the upstream author hasn't yet exposed via predicate or remote interface, and they're treated as transitional — we'd rather delete them as upstream support lands.
231	
232	---
233	
234	## 5. Reporting integration issues
235	
236	If you maintain a mod and want to flag a specific gap, open an issue at https://github.com/bits-orio/multi-team-support/issues with the mod name and a brief description of which handler isn't firing on team surfaces. If you're an admin trying to make a specific combo work, the mod combo plus what doesn't work is enough to triage.

1	# Writing Mods for Multi-Force Environments
2	
3	A short guide for Factorio mod authors who want their mod to keep working when more than one player force exists, or more than one planet-like surface exists. PvP scenarios, team-vs-team modes, per-team-surface setups, and even some single-player overhauls all qualify.
4	
5	Most mods are written assuming the vanilla setup: one player force named `"player"`, one starting surface called `"nauvis"`. That's fine for vanilla play, but a few small habits break the moment a player or scenario adds extra forces or extra surfaces. This page lists the common pitfalls and the cheap fixes.
6	
7	## Mental model
8	
9	Vanilla gives you `game.forces.player` and `game.surfaces.nauvis` by default. Treat both as **examples of a kind**, not as singletons:
10	
11	- Other player-controlled forces can exist (any team scenario, PvP mod, console commands).
12	- Other planet-class surfaces can exist (Space Age planets, mod-added planets, scenario-created copies of nauvis).
13	- A player can switch forces during a game.
14	- A single force can have players spread across many surfaces.
15	
16	If your code says "the player force" or "nauvis" by name, ask whether you actually meant **the acting force** or **the planet nauvis** — they're often different things.
17	
18	Each pattern below shows the pitfall code, why it breaks, and a fix that's a direct rewrite of the same code. Copy whichever shape matches yours.
19	
20	## Which pattern do I need?
21	
22	```mermaid
23	graph TD
24	    Start([Auditing a line of code]) --> Q{What does the line do?}
25	    Q -->|Reads or writes game.forces.player| P1[Pattern 1]
26	    Q -->|Hardcoded surface name or index| P2[Pattern 2]
27	    Q -->|Per-team state in a single value| P3[Pattern 3]
28	    Q -->|Mutates one force, should be all| P4[Pattern 4]
29	    Q -->|Reusable on_event body| P5[Pattern 5]
30	    Q -->|State change others might react to| P6[Pattern 6]
31	```
32	
33	- **Pattern 1** — [Don't hardcode `game.forces.player`](#pattern-1-dont-hardcode-gameforcesplayer)
34	- **Pattern 2** — [Don't hardcode surface names or indices](#pattern-2-dont-hardcode-surface-names-or-indices)
35	- **Pattern 3** — [Key persistent state by force (and by surface)](#pattern-3-key-persistent-state-by-force-and-by-surface)
36	- **Pattern 4** — [Iterate, don't assume singular](#pattern-4-iterate-dont-assume-singular)
37	- **Pattern 5** — [Expose runtime rules so other mods can reuse them](#pattern-5-expose-runtime-rules-so-other-mods-can-reuse-them)
38	- **Pattern 6** — [Emit events for lifecycle hooks](#pattern-6-emit-events-for-lifecycle-hooks)
39	
40	More than one branch may apply to the same line — e.g. a `storage.points[1]` write that *also* assumes the default force can need both Pattern 2 and Pattern 3. In that case, apply both.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## Pattern 1: Don't hardcode `game.forces.player`
45	
46	### Example 1 — Granting a buff after a quest completes
47	
48	**Pitfall:**
49	
50	```lua
51	local function complete_quest(player)
52	    game.forces.player.manual_mining_speed_modifier =
53	        game.forces.player.manual_mining_speed_modifier + 0.25
54	    game.forces.player.print("Quest complete! +25% mining speed.")
55	end
56	```
57	
58	The player who finished the quest is probably on a team force, not the default `"player"` force. The buff lands on an empty force; the print goes to nobody.
59	
60	**Fix:**
61	
62	```lua
63	local function complete_quest(player)
64	    local force = player.force
65	    force.manual_mining_speed_modifier =
66	        force.manual_mining_speed_modifier + 0.25
67	    force.print("Quest complete! +25% mining speed.")
68	end
69	```
70	
71	Use `player.force` — the force that actually earned the reward. Everyone on that team gets the buff and the announcement; everyone on other teams is correctly excluded.
72	
73	### Example 2 — Gating a trade behind research
74	
75	**Pitfall:**
76	
77	```lua
78	local function can_trade(recipe_name)
79	    return game.forces.player.recipes[recipe_name].researched
80	end
81	
82	script.on_event(defines.events.on_gui_click, function(event)
83	    if event.element.name == "trade-belt-button" then
84	        if can_trade("express-belt") then
85	            execute_trade(event.player_index, "express-belt")
86	        end
87	    end
88	end)
89	```
90	
91	The check reads the default force's research, not the clicker's. Teams that already researched express belts get told "no", teams that haven't but where the default force has, get a free pass.
92	
93	**Fix:**
94	
95	```lua
96	local function can_trade(force, recipe_name)
97	    return force.recipes[recipe_name].researched
98	end
99	
100	script.on_event(defines.events.on_gui_click, function(event)
101	    if event.element.name == "trade-belt-button" then
102	        local player = game.get_player(event.player_index)
103	        if can_trade(player.force, "express-belt") then
104	            execute_trade(event.player_index, "express-belt")
105	        end
106	    end
107	end)
108	```
109	
110	The check follows the clicker's force, so each team's trade catalog reflects its own progress.
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Pattern 2: Don't hardcode surface names or indices
115	
116	### Example 1 — Filtering an event handler to "the planet nauvis"
117	
118	**Pitfall:**
119	
120	```lua
121	script.on_event(defines.events.on_built_entity, function(event)
122	    local entity = event.created_entity
123	    if entity.surface.name ~= "nauvis" then return end
124	    if entity.name == "boiler" then
125	        block_build_with_message(event.player_index, "Boilers banned on Nauvis.")
126	        entity.destroy()
127	    end
128	end)
129	```
130	
131	A scenario or multi-surface mod may create extra surfaces that still belong to the nauvis planet (`team-3-nauvis`, `mts-nauvis-3`). The literal-name check rejects all of them, so the rule never fires on those copies and players can build banned items there.
132	
133	**Fix:**
134	
135	```lua
136	script.on_event(defines.events.on_built_entity, function(event)
137	    local entity = event.created_entity
138	    if not (entity.surface.planet
139	            and entity.surface.planet.name == "nauvis") then return end
140	    if entity.name == "boiler" then
141	        block_build_with_message(event.player_index, "Boilers banned on Nauvis.")
142	        entity.destroy()
143	    end
144	end)
145	```
146	
147	`surface.planet.name` identifies the planet itself, not the surface, so the rule fires on every surface that belongs to that planet — including scenario-created copies of nauvis. Skips space platforms automatically (their `planet` is nil). Note that a separate planet prototype derived from nauvis (e.g. a mod that adds a `nauvis-remix` planet) has its own name and won't match — if you want the rule to cover those too, list them explicitly or check against a set of planet names you maintain.
148	
149	> **Caveat — cloned team surfaces have no `.planet` at all.** The engine binds a planet prototype to exactly one surface, so a script-cloned copy of a planet (MTS's team surfaces on the non-Space-Age path, e.g. `team-1-nauvis`) is a plain surface whose `surface.planet` is **nil**. Any feature gated on `surface.planet` silently skips those surfaces — this cost one integrating mod several debugging rounds before the missing gate was found in its logs. When MTS may be present, resolve the planet a surface *represents* through the interface instead:
150	>
151	> ```lua
152	> local function planet_name_of(surface)
153	>     if surface.planet then return surface.planet.name end
154	>     local mts = remote.interfaces["mts-v1"]
155	>     if mts and mts["get_surface_planet"] then
156	>         return remote.call("mts-v1", "get_surface_planet", surface.name)
157	>     end
158	>     return nil -- genuinely planet-less: platforms, lobbies, the landing pen
159	> end
160	> ```
161	>
162	> `get_surface_planet("team-1-nauvis")` returns `"nauvis"`; for surfaces that represent no planet (the landing pen, space platforms) it returns nil, which is usually exactly the skip you want.
163	
164	### Example 2 — Per-surface tint storage
165	
166	**Pitfall:**
167	
168	```lua
169	script.on_init(function()
170	    storage.tints = {
171	        [1]  = settings.global["my-mod-nauvis-color"].value,
172	        [-1] = settings.global["my-mod-space-color"].value,
173	    }
174	end)
175	
176	local function render_chunk(surface, chunk)
177	    rendering.draw_rectangle{
178	        color    = storage.tints[surface.index],
179	        left_top = chunk.area.left_top,
180	        right_bottom = chunk.area.right_bottom,
181	        surface  = surface,
182	    }
183	end
184	```
185	
186	Surface indices are not assigned in a guaranteed order. Another mod creating a surface earlier in load shifts everything — `storage.tints[1]` may not be nauvis. Custom surfaces fall through to `nil` and crash the render call.
187	
188	**Fix:**
189	
190	```lua
191	local DEFAULT_TINT = { r = 0.5, g = 0.5, b = 0.5 }
192	
193	local function tint_for(surface)
194	    local planet = surface.planet and surface.planet.name or "space"
195	    local setting = settings.global["my-mod-" .. planet .. "-color"]
196	    return setting and setting.value or DEFAULT_TINT
197	end
198	
199	script.on_init(function()
200	    storage.tints = {}
201	    for _, surface in pairs(game.surfaces) do
202	        storage.tints[surface.index] = tint_for(surface)
203	    end
204	end)
205	
206	script.on_event(defines.events.on_surface_created, function(event)
207	    local surface = game.surfaces[event.surface_index]
208	    storage.tints[surface.index] = tint_for(surface)
209	end)
210	
211	local function render_chunk(surface, chunk)
212	    rendering.draw_rectangle{
213	        color    = storage.tints[surface.index] or DEFAULT_TINT,
214	        left_top = chunk.area.left_top,
215	        right_bottom = chunk.area.right_bottom,
216	        surface  = surface,
217	    }
218	end
219	```
220	
221	Tint is derived from the *current* surface's planet kind, populated as surfaces appear, and read by the actual current index — no guesses, and unknown surfaces fall back safely instead of crashing.
222	
223	---
224	
225	## Pattern 3: Key persistent state by force (and by surface)
226	
227	### Example 1 — A team score counter
228	
229	**Pitfall:**
230	
231	```lua
232	script.on_init(function()
233	    storage.points = 0
234	end)
235	
236	local function award_points(player, n)
237	    storage.points = storage.points + n
238	    player.print("Total points: " .. storage.points)
239	end
240	```
241	
242	One shared counter. Every team contributes to the same number, so the "score" reflects everyone's combined activity rather than any one team's progress.
243	
244	**Fix:**
245	
246	```lua
247	script.on_init(function()
248	    storage.points = {}
249	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
250	        storage.points[force.index] = 0
251	    end
252	end)
253	
254	script.on_event(defines.events.on_force_created, function(event)
255	    storage.points[event.force.index] = 0
256	end)
257	
258	local function award_points(player, n)
259	    local idx = player.force.index
260	    storage.points[idx] = (storage.points[idx] or 0) + n
261	    player.print("Total points: " .. storage.points[idx])
262	end
263	```
264	
265	Each force gets its own counter, initialized when the force appears and read off the acting player's force.
266	
267	### Example 2 — Per-surface chunk ownership
268	
269	**Pitfall:**
270	
271	```lua
272	script.on_init(function()
273	    storage.claimed = {}  -- claimed[chunk_key] = force_name
274	end)
275	
276	local function claim_chunk(force, surface, chunk_key)
277	    storage.claimed[chunk_key] = force.name
278	end
279	
280	local function owner_of(chunk_key)
281	    return storage.claimed[chunk_key]
282	end
283	```
284	
285	The same chunk key collides across surfaces — claiming `(0,0)` on Vulcanus overwrites whatever claim exists at `(0,0)` on Nauvis. A force on one planet can "steal" another force's chunk on a different planet without ever visiting it.
286	
287	**Fix:**
288	
289	```lua
290	script.on_init(function()
291	    storage.claimed = {}  -- claimed[surface_index][chunk_key] = force_name
292	end)
293	
294	script.on_event(defines.events.on_surface_created, function(event)
295	    storage.claimed[event.surface_index] = {}
296	end)
297	
298	local function claim_chunk(force, surface, chunk_key)
299	    storage.claimed[surface.index] = storage.claimed[surface.index] or {}
300	    storage.claimed[surface.index][chunk_key] = force.name
301	end
302	
303	local function owner_of(surface, chunk_key)
304	    return (storage.claimed[surface.index] or {})[chunk_key]
305	end
306	```
307	
308	Two levels of indexing — surface, then chunk — keep each planet's claims independent. The lookup also takes the surface, so callers can't accidentally drop it.
309	
310	---
311	
312	## Pattern 4: Iterate, don't assume singular
313	
314	### Example 1 — Resetting technology effects after a balance change
315	
316	**Pitfall:**
317	
318	```lua
319	script.on_configuration_changed(function()
320	    game.forces.player.reset_technology_effects()
321	end)
322	```
323	
324	Only the default force gets the recalculation. Team forces keep stale modifiers from the previous mod version — their effective bonuses now drift away from what the new tech tree describes.
325	
326	**Fix:**
327	
328	```lua
329	script.on_configuration_changed(function()
330	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
331	        force.reset_technology_effects()
332	    end
333	end)
334	```
335	
336	Every force gets the recalculation, including enemy and neutral — some mods put research on those forces (for example, evolution-scaled enemy bonuses), so skipping them would leave their modifiers stale too. Vanilla single-force games still work (the loop runs once); multi-force games stay consistent.
337	
338	### Example 2 — Refreshing a per-player GUI when a team value changes
339	
340	**Pitfall:**
341	
342	```lua
343	local function refresh_score_gui(force)
344	    for _, player in pairs(game.players) do
345	        if player.force == force then
346	            local frame = player.gui.screen.score
347	            if frame then
348	                frame.caption = "Score: " .. storage.points[force.index]
349	            end
350	        end
351	    end
352	end
353	```
354	
355	Works, but it's `O(all players)` and easy to forget the `if`. In a 50-player game updating one team's score, this walks 50 players to find the 5 on that team — and any tweak to the loop body is one missed line away from updating *everyone's* GUI.
356	
357	**Fix:**
358	
359	```lua
360	local function refresh_score_gui(force)
361	    for _, player in pairs(force.players) do
362	        local frame = player.gui.screen.score
363	        if frame then
364	            frame.caption = "Score: " .. storage.points[force.index]
365	        end
366	    end
367	end
368	```
369	
370	`force.players` is already the correct subset. Same result, no filter, and the intent reads as "the players on this force" rather than "all players, but really only these."
371	
372	---
373	
374	## Pattern 5: Expose runtime rules so other mods can reuse them
375	
376	The data flow this pattern sets up:
377	
378	```mermaid
379	sequenceDiagram
380	    participant You as Your mod
381	    participant Iface as remote interface
382	    participant Other as Multi-surface mod
383	    Note over You: on_init
384	    You->>Iface: register spill_on_death
385	    Note over Other: needs the rule on its surface
386	    Other->>Iface: call spill_on_death(entity)
387	    Iface->>You: spill_on_death(entity)
388	    You-->>Other: returns
389	```
390	
391	Your existing handler stays in place for the vanilla case; the interface is a second entry point that other mods can drive on demand.
392	
393	### A "spill on death" rule
394	
395	**Pitfall:**
396	
397	```lua
398	script.on_event(defines.events.on_entity_died, function(event)
399	    local entity = event.entity
400	    if entity.surface.name ~= "nauvis" then return end
401	    if entity.type ~= "container" then return end
402	    spill_inventory_to_ground(entity)
403	end)
404	```
405	
406	The behavior is locked inside the handler. A multi-surface mod that wants the same effect on a copy of nauvis cannot reach it without monkey-patching, and the surface filter rejects every alternate nauvis.
407	
408	**Fix:**
409	
410	```lua
411	local function maybe_spill(entity)
412	    if entity.type ~= "container" then return end
413	    spill_inventory_to_ground(entity)
414	end
415	
416	script.on_event(defines.events.on_entity_died, function(event)
417	    if event.entity.surface.name ~= "nauvis" then return end
418	    maybe_spill(event.entity)
419	end)
420	
421	remote.add_interface("my_mod", {
422	    spill_on_death = maybe_spill,
423	})
424	```
425	
426	Behavior is unchanged for the vanilla case. Other mods can now call `remote.call("my_mod", "spill_on_death", entity)` on surfaces you don't know about, reusing your exact logic without copy-pasting it.
427	
428	---
429	
430	## Pattern 6: Emit events for lifecycle hooks
431	
432	The data flow this pattern sets up:
433	
434	```mermaid
435	sequenceDiagram
436	    participant You as Your mod
437	    participant Bus as Factorio event bus
438	    participant Other as Downstream mod
439	    Note over You: on_init generates event id
440	    Note over Other: on_init subscribes
441	    Other->>You: get_event_id
442	    You-->>Other: event_id
443	    Other->>Bus: on_event(event_id, handler)
444	    Note over You: quest completes
445	    You->>Bus: raise_event(event_id, payload)
446	    Bus->>Other: handler(event)
447	```
448	
449	The event id is looked up once, then the downstream mod reacts on its own without polling your storage.
450	
451	### Announcing a quest completion
452	
453	**Pitfall:**
454	
455	```lua
456	local function complete_quest(force, quest_id)
457	    storage.completed[force.index] = storage.completed[force.index] or {}
458	    storage.completed[force.index][quest_id] = true
459	    force.print("Quest complete!")
460	end
461	```
462	
463	If another mod wants to react — award a matching achievement, log to a scoreboard, grant a special item — it has to poll `storage.completed` every tick to notice the change. There's no callback shape.
464	
465	**Fix:**
466	
467	```lua
468	local on_quest_completed = script.generate_event_name()
469	
470	local function complete_quest(force, quest_id)
471	    storage.completed[force.index] = storage.completed[force.index] or {}
472	    storage.completed[force.index][quest_id] = true
473	    force.print("Quest complete!")
474	    script.raise_event(on_quest_completed, {
475	        force_name = force.name,
476	        quest_id   = quest_id,
477	    })
478	end
479	
480	remote.add_interface("my_mod", {
481	    get_event_id = function(name)
482	        if name == "on_quest_completed" then return on_quest_completed end
483	    end,
484	})
485	```
486	
487	Other mods subscribe via `remote.call("my_mod", "get_event_id", "on_quest_completed")` and react inside a normal event handler. No polling, no monkey-patching, and your event payload tells them exactly what happened.
488	
489	---
490	
491	## Quick audit checklist
492	
493	Before tagging a release, grep for these patterns. Each is a near-certain code smell in a multi-force or multi-surface setting:
494	
495	| Pattern in code                        | Likely problem                                                       |
496	|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
497	| `game.forces.player`                   | Use the acting force, or iterate over all player forces.             |
498	| `game.forces["player"]`                | Same.                                                                |
499	| `"nauvis"` as a string literal         | Should this be `surface.planet.name == "nauvis"` instead?            |
500	| `surface.name == "<planet>"`           | Usually wants `surface.planet and surface.planet.name == "<planet>"`.|
501	| Surface index literals (`[1]`, `[-1]`) | Resolve at runtime via `on_surface_created`; never pre-seed.         |
502	| `storage.<x> = <scalar>` for state     | Probably wants `storage.<x>[force.index]` (or `[surface.index]`).    |
503	| `force.print` / `force.add_chart_tag` only on `forces.player` | Use the acting force, or `game.print` for everyone. |
504	
505	For each match, ask: *what would happen if there were five player forces, or three nauvis-class surfaces?* If the answer is "it breaks" or "it silently misbehaves", apply the matching pattern above.
506	
507	---
508	
509	## Why it's worth doing
510	
511	These fixes aren't just for niche scenarios. Each one is a generic correctness improvement that helps:
512	
513	- PvP and team-vs-team scenarios (multiple player forces).
514	- Mods that create extra surfaces (Cargo Ships, Space Exploration-style, scenario-driven copies).
515	- Mods that add extra planet variants in Space Age.
516	- Players who use `/c game.create_force(...)` for their own setups.
517	- Future-you, when you want to add a "challenge mode" force or a second team without rewriting your buff system.
518	
519	In every case, the fix is the same: **stop treating `"player"` and `"nauvis"` as the world, and start treating the *acting* force and the *current* surface as the unit of work.** The code gets shorter, more honest about its assumptions, and works in environments you didn't anticipate.

253	-- ═══ Open Discord Bridge forwarding ═══════════════════════════════════
254	--
255	-- Mirror MTS events to the Open Discord Bridge (interface open-discord-bridge-v1)
256	-- when it is installed. The remote.interfaces guard keeps the bridge an OPTIONAL
257	-- dependency of MTS — nothing breaks if it isn't present.
258	
259	local BRIDGE_INTERFACE = "open-discord-bridge-v1"
260	
261	-- Emoji shown in the bridge's "[mts → …]" category tag, keyed by mts.* event suffix.
262	-- Applied by emit_to_bridge unless the caller passes its own data.label. Emoji rules
263	-- (the bridge sends these to Discord verbatim from a bot):
264	--   • Unicode emoji (🔬, 🚀, …) always render — simplest, no setup.
265	--   • A bare :shortcode: does NOT render from a bot; it shows literally.
266	--   • A CUSTOM emoji must be its raw form <:name:id> AND live on a server the bot is in
267	--     (your own). Other servers' emoji (e.g. the official Factorio server's) won't render,
268	--     regardless of bot permissions — it's server membership, not a permission. Same-server
269	--     custom emoji need no special permission.
270	--   • Get the raw <:name:id>: type "\:lab:" (backslash first) in Discord and send it.
271	local BRIDGE_LABELS = {
272	    research_finished    = "<:lab:1507982217102753962>", -- a :lab: uploaded to our own server
273	    player_joined        = "📥",
274	    player_left          = "📤",
275	    player_joined_team   = "➕",
276	    player_left_team     = "➖",
277	    player_switched_team = "🔀",
278	    team_created         = "🏁",
279	    team_released        = "🏳️",
280	    team_surface_created = "🌎",
281	    milestone_first      = "🥇",
282	    milestone_record     = "⏱️",
283	    rocket_launched      = "🚀",
284	    chat                 = "💬",
285	}
286	
287	--- Emit an arbitrary event to the bridge (no-op if the bridge isn't installed). Fills in
288	--- the category-tag emoji from BRIDGE_LABELS unless the caller already set data.label.
289	function remote_api.emit_to_bridge(event, data)
290	    if remote.interfaces[BRIDGE_INTERFACE] then
291	        data = data or {}
292	        if data.label == nil then
293	            data.label = BRIDGE_LABELS[(event:gsub("^mts%.", ""))]
294	        end
295	        remote.call(BRIDGE_INTERFACE, "emit", { event = event, data = data })
296	    end
297	end
298	
299	--- Declare the mts.* event catalog so the bridge / control plane can offer
300	--- routable toggles without hardcoding MTS. Mutates the bridge's storage, so
301	--- call only from on_init / on_configuration_changed (never from on_load).
302	function remote_api.register_with_bridge()
303	    if not remote.interfaces[BRIDGE_INTERFACE] then return end
304	    remote.call(BRIDGE_INTERFACE, "register_source", {
305	        namespace = "mts",
306	        events = {
307	            { key = "team_created",         description = "A team was created" },
308	            { key = "team_released",        description = "A team was released" },
309	            { key = "player_joined_team",   description = "A player joined a team" },
310	            { key = "player_left_team",     description = "A player left a team" },
311	            { key = "team_surface_created", description = "A team surface was created" },
312	            { key = "milestone_first",      description = "A team set a first-to-produce record" },
313	            { key = "milestone_record",     description = "A team set a production speed record" },
314	            { key = "research_finished",    description = "A team finished a technology" },
315	            { key = "player_joined",        description = "A player joined the game (team-aware)" },
316	            { key = "player_left",          description = "A player left the game (team-aware)" },
317	            { key = "player_switched_team", description = "A player switched teams mid-game" },
318	            { key = "rocket_launched",      description = "A team launched a rocket" },
319	            { key = "chat",                 description = "A chat message (global channel only)" },
320	        },
321	    })
322	    -- We announce these ourselves with team info, so turn off the bridge's team-less
323	    -- baseline versions. The bridge only suppresses a baseline event while we're loaded.
324	    -- "chat" is here for privacy, not enrichment: the bridge's baseline captures EVERY
325	    -- message, but team-only channel messages (scripts/chat_channel.lua) must never
326	    -- reach Discord — events/chat.lua emits the bridge copy for global messages only.
327	    for _, key in ipairs({ "research_finished", "player_joined", "player_left", "rocket_launched", "chat" }) do
328	        remote.call(BRIDGE_INTERFACE, "set_baseline", { event = key, enabled = false })
329	    end
330	end
331	
332	-- ensure_bridge_registered re-applies register_with_bridge once per session. on_init /
333	-- on_configuration_changed don't fire on a plain save reload (no version/mod-list change),
334	-- so a save that was running before the bridge existed — or a content-only mod edit during
335	-- development — would otherwise never (re)disable the baselines. Driving it from on_tick
336	-- (storage mutation is allowed there) makes the registration self-healing every session.
337	-- The flag is a module-load local, so it resets to false on each load.
338	local bridge_registered_this_session = false
339	function remote_api.ensure_bridge_registered()
340	    if bridge_registered_this_session then return end
341	    bridge_registered_this_session = true
342	    remote_api.register_with_bridge()
343	end

345	--- Enrich a raise payload with Discord-friendly names (player + team display name)
346	--- without mutating the original event payload.
347	local function bridge_payload(payload)
348	    local data = {}
349	    for k, v in pairs(payload) do data[k] = v end
350	    if payload.player_index then
351	        local p = game.get_player(payload.player_index)
352	        if p then data.player = p.name end
353	    end
354	    if payload.force_name then
355	        data.team = (storage.team_names or {})[payload.force_name] or payload.force_name
356	    end
357	    return data
358	end

360	--- Build a human-readable sentence for the bridge to show. MTS owns this phrasing;
361	--- the bridge just displays the `text` field. Returns nil for unknown events (the
362	--- bridge then falls back to a key=value summary).
363	local function bridge_text(name, d)
364	    local team = d.team or d.force_name
365	    local who  = d.player or (d.player_index and ("player " .. d.player_index))
366	    if name == "on_team_created" then
367	        return who and string.format("%s created %s", who, team)
368	            or  string.format("%s was created", team)
369	    elseif name == "on_team_released" then
370	        return string.format("%s was released", team)
371	    elseif name == "on_player_joined_team" then
372	        return string.format("%s joined %s", who or "A player", team)
373	    elseif name == "on_player_left_team" then
374	        return string.format("%s left %s", who or "A player", team)
375	    elseif name == "on_team_surface_created" then
376	        return string.format("Surface %s was created for %s", d.surface_name, team)
377	    end
378	    return nil
379	end

382	--
383	-- Called from mts code at the points where the corresponding state
384	-- transition completes. Guarded against missing IDs so commenting an
385	-- event out of `remote_api.events` doesn't crash the callers. Each raise also
386	-- mirrors to the bridge under the mts.* namespace (with the on_ prefix stripped).
387	
388	-- raise() fires the frozen mts-v1 script event for third-party mods and (unless
389	-- opts.no_bridge) mirrors it to the Open Discord Bridge. The force-change events set
390	-- no_bridge because their bridge presentation is handled specially in
391	-- on_player_changed_force (deduped against the connect/disconnect messages).
392	local function raise(name, payload, opts)
393	    opts = opts or {}
394	    payload = payload or {}
395	    local id = remote_api.events[name]
396	    if id then script.raise_event(id, payload) end
397	    if opts.no_bridge then return end
398	    local data = bridge_payload(payload)
399	    data.text = bridge_text(name, data)
400	    remote_api.emit_to_bridge("mts." .. name:gsub("^on_", ""), data)
401	end

70	-- Late-game teams launch rockets continuously (tens of thousands of launches),
71	-- which would flood the Discord bridge. The announcement cadence WIDENS in tiers
72	-- as the running total grows, so the number of posts per tier stays bounded no
73	-- matter how big the base gets:
74	--
75	--   total ≤ 10     every launch      (10 posts)
76	--   total ≤ 100    one per 5         (18 posts: 15, 20, … 100)
77	--   total ≤ 500    one per 25        (16 posts: 125, 150, … 500)
78	--   total ≤ 1000   one per 50        (10 posts: 550, 600, … 1000)
79	--   total > 1000   one per 100       (terminal cadence, forever)
80	--
81	-- So a 45k-launch megabase posts once every ~100 rockets, not the old every-25.
82	-- Each tier is ~10–18 posts, then a flat 1-per-100 — the feed never speeds up
83	-- again past 1000 launches.
84	local ROCKET_TIERS = {
85	    { upto = 10,        step = 1   },
86	    { upto = 100,       step = 5   },
87	    { upto = 500,       step = 25  },
88	    { upto = 1000,      step = 50  },
89	    { upto = math.huge, step = 100 },
90	}

93	local function rocket_announce_step(total)
94	    for _, tier in ipairs(ROCKET_TIERS) do

96	    end
97	    return 100  -- unreachable: the math.huge tier catches everything; defensive
98	end

100	-- Report the HIGHEST step-multiple the counter has reached that hasn't been
101	-- announced yet, rather than testing `total % step == 0`. Two engine realities:
102	--   • force.rockets_launched skips and duplicates values when several rockets
103	--     resolve close together (live logs show "...30254, 30254, 30256..."), so a
104	--     plain exact-multiple test goes silent when the multiple is skipped and
105	--     double-posts when a duplicate lands on one.
106	--   • the announced number should read cleanly, not as a raw overshoot (…45301).
107	-- floor(total/step)*step is the highest multiple the counter has reached; report
108	-- it whenever it exceeds the last reported mark. The feed never goes silent,
109	-- never double-posts, and every announced number past 10 is a step multiple
110	-- (…45300, 45400) — always ending in 0 or 5. Deriving the mark from the CURRENT
111	-- total (not last+step) also means a fresh install / counter reset on an already-
112	-- huge force jumps straight to the current neighbourhood instead of crawling up
113	-- from a low number. A tier boundary widens the step, so the next mark lands on
114	-- the wider grid (after 100 the next is 125, after 1000 it's 1100).
115	--- @return integer|nil  the mark reached — the highest unannounced step multiple
116	---   past 10, or the raw count at/below 10 — or nil when no new mark is due.
117	local function rocket_announce_mark(last, total)
118	    if total < last then return total end          -- counter reset (force recreated): re-arm on raw count
119	    if total <= 10 then                            -- pre-alignment tier: every launch, raw count
120	        return (total > last) and total or nil
121	    end
122	    local step = rocket_announce_step(total)
123	    local mark = math.floor(total / step) * step   -- highest step multiple the counter has reached
124	    return (mark > last) and mark or nil
125	end
